HP OmniBook X Flip 2-in-1 14" 2K OLED Touchscreen Laptop -Silver (Intel Core Ultra 7 355/ 16GB LPDDR5X/ 2TB SSD/ Intel Graphics/ Copilot+ PC/ Backlit Keyboard/ Windows 11 Home)

reviews.quote: Flexible performance with AMD Zen 5. Pros: portable and travel-friendly USB-C AC adapter, strong CPU performance for the size, full sRGB colors at minimum, integrated HDMI and USB-A, strong chassis design, great battery life. Cons: HDR only available on highest-end SKU, no Arc B390 or Radeon 890M options, 1200p OLED panel could be brighter, new keyboard takes getting used to. (NBC review of the OmniBook X Flip 14 AMD Zen 5 config.)

praises: 2K OLED makes this the best-looking screen in any sub-$2,500 CA convertible right now
Deep blacks with no backlight bleed — excellent for dark-room movie watching in tent mode
Great battery life for a convertible — Panther Lake sips power in light browsing and video
Light (~1.4 kg) and thin for a 2-in-1; easy tablet/tent use
1TB storage at this price beats the IPS tier's value once discounts stack
complaints: Only 16GB soldered RAM — no upgrade path
OLED glossy touch glass reflects badly in bright rooms
HP bloatware (Support Assistant, Maxx Audio) ships preinstalled and annoys owners
60Hz panel — competitors at this price are moving to 120Hz
Regular price $2,719 is poor value; only the frequent ~$540 sales make sense

design_philosophy: The OLED tier is the OmniBook X Flip 14 as HP intends it to be experienced: the Spectre x360's gem-cut premium spirit reborn as a clean aluminum convertible with a vivid OLED touch panel aimed at media-first buyers who also want pen input and Copilot+ AI.
rating_notes: Pro score attached from NBC review of the OmniBook X Flip 14 AMD Zen 5 config (86%, gap-fill 2026-11-24); this Intel Ultra 355 tier shares chassis/display/battery findings but the score is from the AMD sibling.
